quests.instruction: Write a capital B next to a lowercase d, then a capital P next to a lowercase q.
quests.question: B d P q
quests.hint: Capital B and P are stem letters with bumps on the right. Lowercase d has its bump on the left of the stem and q has its stem below.
quests.explanation: Letters that look alike across cases are easy to mix up. Remember: capitals have the stem first, lowercase d and q have the circle first.
quests.funFact: Teachers often use touch, sight and sound together because children remember letters better that way.

quests.instruction: Write a lowercase d next to a capital B, then a lowercase q next to a capital P.
quests.question: d B q P
quests.hint: Take your time with each switch from small to tall. d's stem goes up, q's stem goes down.
quests.explanation: Switching case and shape in alternate letters trains your hand to choose a letter shape on purpose.
quests.funFact: Fingertips have many touch sensors, which is why people can feel tiny raised Braille dots.

quests.instruction: Write a lowercase b next to a capital D, then a lowercase p next to a capital Q.
quests.question: b D p Q
quests.hint: b is a stem and bump, D is a stem and a big curve. p's stem drops below, and Q has a tail.
quests.explanation: Alternating case gives your hand a different job with every letter. Keep your heights tidy.
quests.funFact: Louis Braille developed his system of raised dots when he was a teenager.

quests.instruction: Write the lowercase letters m, n, r, h and u in a row. Keep the arches and cups even.
quests.question: m n r h u
quests.hint: m, n, r and h use arches, u uses a cup. Make every arch the same size. h is taller than the others.
quests.explanation: Arches and cups are mirror shapes. Writing them together trains your hand to switch from one to the other.
quests.funFact: Long ago, scribes often wrote the letter u where we would write v.

quests.instruction: Write the capital letters M, N, H and U in a row.
quests.question: M N H U
quests.hint: M has a zigzag, N has one slant, H has a bar and U has a cup. Each starts with a stem except U's cup.
quests.explanation: The capitals are all tall, with stems and slants. Heights should be the same and the spaces equal.
quests.funFact: The capital letters H, I, N, O, S, X and Z look the same when turned upside down.

quests.instruction: Write m, then capital N, then r, then capital H, then u, taking turns between small and tall.
quests.question: m N r H u
quests.hint: Switch your mindset with each letter: small arch, tall slanted N, small half-arch, tall H, small cup.
quests.explanation: Alternating sizes makes you think about heights every time, a real challenge for handwriting control.
quests.funFact: Japanese is written with three kinds of characters: hiragana, katakana and kanji.

quests.instruction: Write the five vowel letters in lowercase: a, e, i, o, u.
quests.question: a e i o u
quests.hint: Make a, e and o as round letters, i as a short stem with a dot, and u as a cup with a stem. Keep all the same height.
quests.explanation: Vowel letters make the open sounds in words, and writing them together shows your small-letter control.
quests.funFact: The five vowel letters of English are a, e, i, o and u, and sometimes y acts like a vowel too.

quests.instruction: Write the five vowel letters in capitals: A, E, I, O, U.
quests.question: A E I O U
quests.hint: A: roof and bar. E: three bars. I: stem with bars. O: circle. U: cup. Keep them all tall.
quests.explanation: Capital vowels vary from slanted to round. This is a good test of switching between stroke types.
quests.funFact: Spanish uses each vowel letter for one steady sound, which makes many words easy to spell from how they sound.

quests.instruction: Write the vowels, taking turns between lowercase and capital: a, E, i, O, u.
quests.question: a E i O u
quests.hint: Small a, tall E, small i with its dot, tall O, small u. Keep the baseline level.
quests.explanation: Alternating case is hard. Check the heights as you go and keep every letter on the baseline.
quests.funFact: English has around twenty vowel sounds, even though it has only five vowel letters.

quests.instruction: Write these consonants in lowercase: b, c, d, f, g.
quests.question: b c d f g
quests.hint: b, d and f have tall stems, c is a small open curve, and g has a descender. Check each height.
quests.explanation: Five letters, three different heights: tall, small and descending. Choosing the right height for each is the challenge.
quests.funFact: English has 21 consonant letters and five vowel letters.

quests.instruction: Write the same consonants in capitals: B, C, D, F, G.
quests.question: B C D F G
quests.hint: B and D start with stems, C and G start with curves, F has two bars. Keep the capitals the same height.
quests.explanation: Capitals are all the same height, so the shape does the work. Keep your curves round and your bars level.
quests.funFact: The word 'rhythm' has no a, e, i, o or u in it.

quests.instruction: Write b, C, d, F, g, alternating lowercase and capital.
quests.question: b C d F g
quests.hint: Tall b, tall C, tall d, tall F, but small g with a tail. Watch which ones are capitals.
quests.explanation: Capitals and lowercase letters can have the same height when they have ascenders. Pay attention to g, which drops below the line.
quests.funFact: The word 'strengths' has nine letters but only one vowel.

quests.instruction: Write these lowercase letters: h, j, k, l, m, n.
quests.question: h j k l m n
quests.correctAnswer: h j k l m n
quests.hint: h, k and l are tall, j has a tail and a dot, m and n are small arches. Remember the height of each.
quests.explanation: A mix of tall letters, small letters and a tail. Writing them in a row tests all three heights.
quests.funFact: Czech adds small marks above letters, such as the č in the word 'česky'.

quests.instruction: Write H, J, K, L, M, N in capitals.
quests.question: H J K L M N
quests.correctAnswer: H J K L M N
quests.hint: H and N join two stems, J hooks, K has slants, L is a corner, M zigzags. Keep heights equal.
quests.explanation: Six capitals, all stems. Spacing them evenly makes the row look tidy.
quests.funFact: On a phone keypad, the letters J, K and L share the number 5.

quests.instruction: Write h, J, k, L, m, N, taking turns between small and capital.
quests.question: h J k L m N
quests.correctAnswer: h J k L m N
quests.hint: Check each one: h and k are tall lowercase letters, J, L and N are capitals, m is small.
quests.explanation: Mixed case is harder than same-case rows. Take time and go step by step.
quests.funFact: Old phone keypads put three or four letters on each number key, so people could spell words as phone numbers.

quests.instruction: Write these lowercase letters: p, q, r, s, t, v.
quests.question: p q r s t v
quests.correctAnswer: p q r s t v
quests.hint: p and q drop below the line, r, s and v are small, t is a bit taller. Keep descenders level.
quests.explanation: Descenders, small letters and a medium-height letter all in one line. Plan heights as you go.
quests.funFact: When you say 'pop' with a hand in front of your mouth, you can feel a small puff of air on the p.

quests.instruction: Write P, Q, R, S, T, V in capitals.
quests.question: P Q R S T V
quests.correctAnswer: P Q R S T V
quests.hint: P and R have bumps, Q has a tail, S curves, T has a bar, V is a point. Keep all the same height.
quests.explanation: Capital letters look more complex, but the same height keeps them tidy.
quests.funFact: Libraries shelve books in alphabetical order by the author's last name.

quests.instruction: Write p, Q, r, S, t, V, alternating lowercase and capital.
quests.question: p Q r S t V
quests.correctAnswer: p Q r S t V
quests.hint: Lowercase p has a tail, capital Q has a tail. r is small, S is tall. t is medium, V is tall.
quests.explanation: Alternating letters from the same family keeps your memory of both sizes sharp.
quests.funFact: The word 'typewriter' can be typed using only the top row of letters on a keyboard.

quests.instruction: Write these lowercase letters: w, x, y, z.
quests.question: w x y z
quests.hint: w, x and z sit between the middle line and the baseline. y drops below. All are slants.
quests.explanation: These four letters are all slants. Keep the angles steady and the heights even.
quests.funFact: In the radio spelling alphabet W is 'Whiskey', X is 'X-ray', Y is 'Yankee' and Z is 'Zulu'.

quests.instruction: Write W, X, Y, Z in capitals.
quests.question: W X Y Z
quests.hint: All four reach the top line and the baseline. Slant carefully and keep spaces between them.
quests.explanation: Pointed capitals need sharp corners. Keep your pen steady at each point.
quests.funFact: There are about seven thousand languages spoken in the world.

quests.instruction: Write w, X, y, Z, taking turns between small and capital, then finish with x and W.
quests.question: w X y Z x W
quests.correctAnswer: w X y Z x W
quests.hint: Check heights: lowercase w, y, x are small, capitals X, Z, W are tall. y still has a tail.
quests.explanation: Six letters of mixed sizes need constant checking. Slow down at each switch.
quests.funFact: On a computer, a capital A is stored as the number 65 in a common code called ASCII.

quests.instruction: Write this pattern three times in a row: a small a, then a capital A.
quests.question: aA aA aA
quests.hint: Write a small a, then a capital A, then repeat. Keep the rhythm steady: small, tall, small, tall.
quests.explanation: Repeating a pattern tests your consistency. Each repeat should look the same as the first.
quests.funFact: Computers treat capital and lowercase letters as different characters, which is why passwords are case-sensitive.

quests.instruction: Write the pattern: m, M, n, N, m, M.
quests.question: mM nN mM
quests.hint: Small arches and tall zigzags take turns. Keep your tall letters the same height.
quests.explanation: Patterns with alternating sizes give you a feeling of rhythm.
quests.funFact: Calligraphers practice the same stroke again and again to make their letters even.

quests.instruction: Write the pattern: e, E, o, O, e, E, o, O.
quests.question: eE oO eE oO
quests.hint: Small round, tall round, taking turns. Make every capital exactly the same height.
quests.explanation: Round letters in two sizes are a great test of size control.
quests.funFact: Scribes in monasteries decorated the first letter on a page of a manuscript with gold and bright colors.

quests.instruction: Look at k, R, t, M. Cover them and write them in order from memory.
quests.question: k R t M
quests.hint: Picture each letter's shape and size. Lowercase k is tall, R is a capital with a leg, t is a medium letter, M has a zigzag.
quests.explanation: Writing mixed letters from memory is a stronger test than copying. Mistakes show what to practice next.
quests.funFact: Practising a little each day helps you remember things better than one long session.

quests.instruction: Look at G, a, Q, d. Cover them and write them in order from memory.
quests.question: G a Q d
quests.hint: G: C with a shelf. a: circle and short stem. Q: circle and tail. d: circle and tall stem.
quests.explanation: Alternating capitals and lowercase makes you retrieve each shape on its own, which makes memory stronger.
quests.funFact: Sleep helps the brain keep what it learned during the day.

quests.instruction: Look at y, B, f, W, z. Cover them and write them in order from memory.
quests.question: y B f W z
quests.hint: y: tail below the line. B: stem and two bumps. f: tall with a bar. W: four slants. z: bar, slant, bar.
quests.explanation: Five mixed letters from memory. If one was tricky, trace it later.
quests.funFact: A person's handwriting can change over their lifetime.

quests.instruction: Write the first, middle and last letters of the alphabet, each as a capital and a lowercase pair.
quests.question: Aa Mm Zz
quests.hint: Aa: roof and circle. Mm: zigzag and two arches. Zz: bar, slant, bar in two sizes.
quests.explanation: Three pairs from the two ends and the middle of the alphabet test your range, from slants to arches.
quests.funFact: The Latin alphabet is the most widely used writing system in the world.

quests.instruction: Write four stem letters, each in capital and lowercase: B, D, P and R.
quests.question: Bb Dd Pp Rr
quests.hint: All start with a stem. b and d have tall stems, p has a stem going down, r is a small half arch.
quests.explanation: Stem and bump letters were tricky earlier. If you write them clearly now, you really have them.
quests.funFact: Before printing, copying a single book by hand could take months.

quests.instruction: Write four letters that need extra room below the line, each as a capital and lowercase pair: G, J, Q, Y.
quests.question: Gg Jj Qq Yy
quests.hint: Capitals stay above the baseline and the lowercase letters drop below. Give each pair space.
quests.explanation: Descenders are the hardest part of a long line of writing. Keeping them even is real control.
quests.funFact: A 'font' was once a set of metal letters of one size and style.
